cards.title: World Notes: Rowing Through Rough Water
cards.sub: A real person and place behind this week's game
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: A rowing boat moves when people pull long oars through the water. In big waves, it takes strength and good timing to keep the boat steady.
Grace and her father rowed a coble, a heavy wooden boat built for the rough North Sea. The real boat is kept today at the Grace Darling Museum in Bamburgh, England.
When they reached the rock, her father climbed out to help the people, and Grace held the boat steady by herself.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Today you collect your best details from both texts.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build words, fix a sentence like an editor, and build long words.
transcripts.guide2: Read both texts again. Then answer the questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you write one paragraph for each text.

notes.wordParts: Prefixes and suffixes from this year: re- = again, un- = not, trans- = across, inter- = between, -ful = full of, -less = without.
notes.grammar: Year review: capitals for names and the first word, a comma after an opening part, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, and irregular past forms like went and took.
notes.spelling: Long words: find the vowels, split between them, read each chunk, then push the chunks together. Rescue = res + cue.
notes.wgrd: A comparison needs a detail from each text, and a sentence that shows how they connect. Mira’s words echo Text 1’s idea of courage.
vocab: having or showing courage; willing to act even when afraid
continuing to try even when things are hard
a quality that shows good character

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Is someone being brave?

items.t: Mira says, “Leave him alone,” and her voice comes out steadier than she expected.
items.why: She speaks up for someone smaller, even while she is afraid.

items.t: The three big boys take younger children's things for weeks.
items.why: Picking on smaller kids is not courage.

items.t: Text 1 says courage is something you practice, one choice at a time.
items.why: Every brave choice makes the next one easier.
